criterion: Across the marketing pages and the workspace one near-black carries text, borders and dividers, with a single light vivid blue on links and brand plates.
evaluation_rule: The product uses one dark neutral at several strengths for every piece of text, every border and every divider, and exactly one saturated hue anywhere in the chrome. Yes if a reader sees a single dark neutral doing the text and line work and a single saturated hue confined to links, accents and brand artwork. No if a second dark family appears alongside the first, or a second saturated hue appears in the chrome.

criterion: The workspace reserves four accent colours for meaning, with a named grey ladder used only on mock surfaces and drawn logos.
evaluation_rule: The four meanings are something that worked, something gone wrong, something in progress and a plain category. A GREY LADDER is a set of named neutral steps from lightest to darkest. Yes if each of the four meanings owns an accent that appears nowhere else, and the grey steps appear only behind mock surfaces or inside drawn logos. No if an accent is reused for an unrelated state, or a grey step sets body text.

criterion: Display headlines on the marketing pages are set in a serif face that appears nowhere else, with navigation labels in an uppercase letterspaced monospace face.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the large marketing headlines are the only serif in the product and the header navigation labels are uppercase monospace with visibly loose letterspacing. No if the serif also sets body copy or interface text, or if navigation labels share the face used for body copy.

criterion: Every illustration in the product is drawn or generated by code, with company logos as monogram tiles, person avatars as initials circles and the trusted-by strip as plain text wordmarks.
evaluation_rule: A MONOGRAM TILE is a square carrying one or two letters. Yes if no photographic or vector image file appears anywhere and every logo, avatar, plate and texture is drawn by the running product. No if any illustration is a stored image file, or if a company logo, an avatar or a trusted-by mark is anything other than a drawn substitute.

criterion: Each product demonstration on the marketing pages sits inside a drawn window frame carrying three traffic dots and a centred title.
evaluation_rule: Yes if every embedded product mock is wrapped in a small drawn window chrome with three dots along one edge and a title centred above the content. No if a mock sits directly on the page with no window frame, or if the frame is missing the dots or the centred title.

criterion: A boolean cell in the workspace table shows a mark beside a word, and the landing page Problem band names two tradeoffs.
evaluation_rule: Yes if every true or false cell renders a check or a cross together with the matching word, and the Problem band presents exactly two named tradeoffs. No if a boolean cell shows only a mark, or the Problem band names fewer or more than two tradeoffs.

criterion: Each marketing page and each workspace object view leads with a single primary action that is visually distinct from every secondary one.
evaluation_rule: A PRIMARY ACTION is the one thing the page most wants somebody to do, such as Get started on a marketing page or the New control on an object view. Yes if exactly one control per page wears the strongest treatment on the page. No if two or more controls share the strongest treatment on one page, or if no control stands out from the rest.

criterion: Buttons, chips, cell editors and rail items in the workspace each show a resting, a pointed-at, a pressed, a focused and an unavailable appearance, with the unavailable state carrying more than a colour change.
evaluation_rule: Yes if pointing at, pressing and focusing one of these controls each changes how the control looks, and an unavailable control is marked by something beyond its colour, such as a label or a struck treatment. No if any of the five states looks identical to another, or if unavailability is signalled by colour alone.

criterion: Opening the command palette moves keyboard focus into the palette, and closing the palette returns focus to whatever opened the palette.
evaluation_rule: Yes if keyboard focus lands inside the overlay the moment the overlay opens and returns to the control or surface that opened the overlay when the overlay closes. No if focus stays behind the overlay while the overlay is open, or lands at the top of the page after the overlay closes.

criterion: A row edited by another person in the workspace table is announced to assistive technology as the change arrives.
evaluation_rule: ANNOUNCED means a screen reader speaks the change without the reader moving focus. Yes if a remote edit produces a spoken announcement naming the change. No if a remote edit changes the row silently.

criterion: Movement on the landing page and in the workspace shares one eased character, with a reduced-motion preference leaving each scene standing finished.
evaluation_rule: EASED means movement leaves quickly and arrives slowly. Yes if movement across the marketing pages and the workspace reads as one family, and a reduced-motion preference leaves every mock standing finished with nothing looping. No if one surface moves with a visibly different character from another, or a mock keeps looping under a reduced-motion preference.

criterion: Body text across the marketing pages and the workspace meets WCAG AA contrast against the background, with every control reachable by keyboard and marked by a visible focus ring.
evaluation_rule: Yes if body copy clears the WCAG AA contrast bar against the surface behind the copy and a keyboard alone reaches every control with a focus ring visible at each stop. No if body copy sits below the bar on any surface, or if a control is reachable only by pointer, or if a focused control shows no ring.

criterion: At tablet width the workspace rail collapses to icons, and every marketing page fits its own width at every size between phone and desk.
evaluation_rule: Yes if narrowing the window to tablet width leaves the rail as a column of icons and every page keeps its content inside the window at every width between phone and desk. No if the rail keeps its labels at tablet width, or if a page grows a sideways scrollbar at some width.

criterion: Decoration stands in place of content on a marketing band.
evaluation_rule: DECORATION is artwork or ornament occupying space that carries no product information. Yes if a marketing band is filled with ornament where the product information belongs. No if every band carries product information in the space the band occupies.

criterion: The workspace presents an oversized marketing hero above the object views.
evaluation_rule: An OVERSIZED MARKETING HERO is a large promotional banner of the kind used on a public landing page. Yes if a signed-in object view opens with such a banner above the records. No if the signed-in object view opens on the records themselves.
